title: ZIF-8 Nanoparticle for Gene Delivery in Sperm-Mediated Gene Transfer
author: Sameni, Moradbeigi, et al.
materials: To determine the copy number of plasmid in the sperm nucleolus, it is necessary to extract the sperm genome. To accomplish this, the spermatozoa of mice 106 were subjected to different concentrations of ZIF-8 containing 7.5, 15, 30, and 60 ug mL −1, along with a control group (sperm incubated in HTF). The plasmid concentration used was 20 ng ul−1(Plasmid pCAG-eCAS9-GFP-U6-gRNA). The incubation was performed for 30 min at 37.5 °C with 5% (v/v) CO2 in the air with high humidity. Following the incubation period, the sperm was retrieved and thoroughly rinsed three times in a phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) solution using centrifugation at 600 g for five minutes. Subsequently,20 U of DNase I (Invitrogen) was applied to the sperm for 30 min to remove exogenous DNA adsorbed on the sperm surface but not internalized. Following the DNaseI treatment, the sperm were washed three additional times in PBS (Ca2 + and Mg2 + free) via centrifugation for 5 min at 600 g, and the sperm pellet was utilized to extract DNA using a genome extraction kit.

steps.title: Characterize ZIF‑8 nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Perform morphological, structural, and size analyses of the synthesized ZIF‑8 nanoparticles using the listed instruments and settings.

substeps.instruction: Coat a small amount of ZIF‑8 powder with gold under vacuum and image it with a scanning electron microscope (SEM FEI Quanta 200).
Record the infrared spectrum of ZIF‑8 on a JASCO FT/IR‑4600 spectrometer over the range 400–4000 cm⁻¹ to identify functional groups.
Measure the hydrodynamic size distribution of ZIF‑8 by Dynamic Light Scattering using a DLS‑nanoPartica (Model SZ‑100 series, HORIBA).
Obtain the X‑ray diffraction pattern of ZIF‑8 on a Philips PW 1730 diffractometer to assess crystal structure.

steps.title: Prepare ZIF‑8 working solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the ZIF‑8 stock (1 mg mL⁻¹) to obtain the required test concentrations for sperm incubation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare ZIF‑8 solutions at 7.5, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, and 200 µg mL⁻¹ by appropriate volumetric dilution of the 1 mg mL⁻¹ stock.
Prepare a positive‑control solution containing 3 % (v/v) DMSO.
Prepare a negative‑control solution consisting of sperm medium (HTF) without ZIF‑8.

steps.title: Incubate sperm with ZIF‑8
steps.instruction: Expose mouse spermatozoa to each ZIF‑8 concentration and controls for 30 minutes under standard incubation conditions.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot equal volumes of sperm suspension into separate tubes for each ZIF‑8 concentration, the DMSO control, and the HTF control.
Add the corresponding ZIF‑8 solution (or DMSO/HTF) to each tube to achieve the target concentration.
Incubate all tubes for 30 min at the laboratory‑maintained temperature and humidity (conditions identical for all samples).

steps.title: Prepare exogenous CRISPR plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Cultivate and purify the pCAG‑eCAS9‑GFP‑U6‑gRNA plasmid for use in complex formation.

substeps.instruction: Transform Stbl4 competent E. coli with the plasmid and grow overnight in selective medium.
Harvest bacterial cells and isolate plasmid DNA using the FavorPrep™ DNA extraction kit (Taiwan) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Form ZIF‑8NP‑DNA complexes
steps.instruction: Combine ZIF‑8 nanoparticles with the purified CRISPR plasmid to generate delivery complexes.

substeps.instruction: For each ZIF‑8 concentration prepared earlier, mix the ZIF‑8 suspension with the plasmid DNA and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Add CRISPR plasmid to a final concentration of 20 ng µL⁻¹ to each mixture.
Incubate the mixtures for an additional 30 min in an incubator (temperature as used for sperm incubation).

steps.title: Extract sperm genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate DNA from sperm that have been treated with ZIF‑8 to assess plasmid uptake.

substeps.instruction: Treat sperm (previously incubated with 7.5, 15, 30, or 60 µg mL⁻¹ ZIF‑8, plus an HTF control) with 20 ng µL⁻¹ plasmid for 30 min at 37.5 °C, 5 % CO₂, high humidity.
Centrifuge the sperm at 600 g for 5 min and discard supernatant; wash the pellet three times with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) by repeating the centrifugation step.
Add 20 U of DNase I (Invitrogen) to the washed sperm and incubate 30 min to degrade any DNA bound to the sperm surface.
Wash the DNase‑treated sperm three additional times with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free PBS, centrifuging 5 min at 600 g each wash.
Extract genomic DNA from the final sperm pellet using a commercial genome extraction kit, following the kit’s instructions.
